blocks.md: **On a family-income basis the US ranks 40th most unequal of 150 countries (Gini 45.0) — far above Western Europe and the Nordics, well below southern Africa and much of Latin America.**

| Rank (1 = least equal) | Country | Gini |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Lesotho | 63.2 |
| 2 | South Africa | 62.5 |
| 5 | Haiti | 60.8 |
| 10 | Colombia | 53.5 |
| 30 | China | 46.6 |
| 40 | United States | 45.0 |
| 111 | United Kingdom | 32.4 |
| 112 | Canada | 32.1 |
| 132 | Denmark | 28.8 |
| 139 | Norway | 26.8 |
| 145 | Sweden | 24.9 |
| 150 | Finland | 21.5 |

The US is 45.0 here but ≈ 0.64 in [US Income Inequality Since 1917](note:us-income-inequality-since-1917). The **variable** (family income vs tax-unit income) and the **population** (households vs tax filers) differ, and survey years vary by country. Comparing Ginis across sources without checking these is a classic error — the core point of [Defining Inequality](note:defining-inequality).
